description:
The PLAN.md and workspace AGENTS.md extras-preservation policy say "every
public method-argument struct in this crate that appears on the JMAP wire
carries an `extra` field" and that field MUST round-trip on the wire.

In this crate, two divergent behaviors ship today:

  Iterate-merge (extras DO reach the wire — but with the clobber bug from
  bd:JMAP-tjvm.1 and bd:JMAP-tjvm.2):
    - email_get / email_parse (use `for (k,v) in serde_json::to_value(p).map`)

  Typed-field-only (extras are SILENTLY DROPPED — they never reach the wire):
    - email_copy (email.rs:208-228) — reads `from_account_id`,
      `on_success_destroy_original`, `destroy_from_if_in_state`; ignores
      `params.extra`
    - mailbox_set (mailbox.rs:82-114) — reads `on_destroy_remove_emails`;
      ignores `params.extra`
    - email_submission_set (submission.rs:160-208) — reads
      `on_success_update_email`, `on_success_destroy_email`; ignores
      `params.extra`

The round-trip tests in methods/mod.rs (e.g.
`email_copy_params_propagates_vendor_extras`) only verify that the *struct*
serializes the extra key. They do NOT verify the extras reach the wire when
the struct is used through the production method. This is why the
drop-on-the-wire branch has never been caught.

Impact: a vendor that puts a private field in `MailboxSetParams.extra`
expecting RFC-style round-trip per workspace policy will see it disappear
between caller and server. Silent data loss exactly the policy was designed
to prevent.

This finding is the policy-implementation gap. Fix it together with
bd:JMAP-tjvm.1 and bd:JMAP-tjvm.2 so the merge is exactly-once and exactly-
correct everywhere: typed args owned by the builder, extras flattened
beneath, and a wiremock end-to-end test per method that asserts extras
reach the wire.

Canonical-template propagation: same shape will exist in every extension-
client sibling. Audit/fix in lockstep.
title: Extras policy inconsistency: silently dropped in email_copy / mailbox_set / email_submission_set
